h1: Loei Palace Hotel — the big city hotel in central Loei where rooms run larger than the price suggests
intro: Loei town does not have many large hotels, and among them Loei Palace Hotel is the name that comes up most when you want a central base with a pool, a gym and genuinely big rooms · a 4-star, 156-room hotel set right beside Kut Pong public park, a few minutes' walk from the Saturday Walking Street · rooms from approx ฿900/night, which many guests say buys more floor space than they expected at this price.

Spacious warm-toned guest room with a large bed overlooking the park

body.html: What sets Loei Palace apart from most places to stay in central Loei is that it is a full 156-room hotel, not a guesthouse or a converted shophouse · there is a wide lobby, an outdoor pool, a gym and on-site restaurants · it opened in 1999 and had a major refurbishment around 2012, so the building reads as an older-generation hotel but one kept in good shape — a point many reviews agree on, calling it dated but clean rather than run-down.

What guests like most is the room size · even an entry-level Deluxe is around 41 square metres with a large bed and a roomy bathroom, and the line runs up through 63-square-metre Grand Deluxe rooms to Family Rooms and suites of 72–112 square metres · for a starting rate often under a thousand baht, that is rare floor space in Loei town · many reviews note it suits families or self-drivers heading up to Phu Kradueng or Phu Ruea who want a comfortable bed in town before or after the mountains.
"The room was far bigger than I expected, big bed, clean bathroom — at this price in Loei it's great value. Quick check-in and lovely staff."

Location scores well too · the hotel sits right next to Kut Pong public park, so a few steps takes you to a place for a morning walk or run · it is about 400 metres from the Saturday Walking Street, an easy stroll, and a short drive from the town's markets and restaurants · Loei Airport is roughly 5.7 km away, so onward travel is simple · for anyone using Loei town as a base before Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea or Phu Kradueng, a central spot like this makes it easy to repack and start the trip.

On food and facilities, the hotel has Botun restaurant serving Thai and local Loei dishes, plus Wine De Bay · breakfast is a buffet that most reviews pass as fine — a reasonable spread and decent flavours, even if it is not a big-city luxury buffet · the outdoor pool and gym are extras you rarely find at similarly priced places in Loei town · free, generous parking is a clear advantage for self-drivers.

Honestly, this is not a new-design or modern boutique hotel · the recurring gripes are air-conditioning that does not cool evenly in some rooms, a few aging bathroom fittings in keeping with the building's age, and stretches when the pool is closed for maintenance · the overall styling is older-generation rather than contemporary · but if what you are after is a big, clean room, a central location, a pool and parking at a price many call good value — Loei Palace delivers, and its 9.0 from 106 Trip.com reviews reflects that.

A tip from reading a lot of reviews here: ask for a Grand Deluxe or an upper-floor room facing the park for a greener, quieter outlook than the road side · if you travel during the Phi Ta Khon festival (June–July) or in the cool season when Phu Kradueng and Phu Ruea draw crowds, rooms fill fast, so book several weeks ahead and lock in free cancellation.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Loei Palace Hotel

faq.q: Where is Loei Palace Hotel and what is nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is at 167/4 Charoen Rat Road, Kut Pong, Mueang Loei, Loei province · it sits right next to Kut Pong public park, a few steps away · it is about 400 metres from the Saturday Walking Street and roughly 5.7 km from Loei Airport · a central spot well suited as a base before Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea or Phu Kradueng.

faq.q: How much does Loei Palace Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿900/night for a 41-sqm Deluxe · a Grand Deluxe (63 sqm) runs around ฿1,200 · Family Rooms and the One Bedroom Suite (72 sqm) climb to roughly ฿1,800–2,200 · prices vary by season and festivals, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Loei Palace Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits families and self-drivers who want a big, clean room, a central location, a pool and free parking · it works well as a base before or after Phu Kradueng, Phu Ruea or Chiang Khan · it is less ideal for travellers set on a new, modern-design hotel.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Loei Palace really spacious?
faq.a: Yes · even an entry-level Deluxe is around 41 sqm with a large bed and roomy bathroom, and rooms run from a 63-sqm Grand Deluxe up to 72–112-sqm suites · room size is the single most talked-about point in reviews and the main reason many call it good value in Loei town.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book and can I cancel?
faq.a: During the Phi Ta Khon festival (June–July) and the cool season when Phu Kradueng and Phu Ruea draw crowds, book several weeks ahead as rooms fill fast · every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose that if your plans are not yet firm.

faq.q: What are breakfast and the pool like?
faq.a: Breakfast is a buffet at Botun restaurant with a reasonable choice and decent flavours · there is an outdoor pool and a gym on site · note the pool is closed for maintenance at times, so if swimming matters, check its status with the hotel before booking.
